name: Euljiro Nogari Alley - Eulsooni
description: A neighborhood institution in Euljiro's dried-pollack beer alley. The crispy fried nogari paired with cold draft beer is the star combo, loved by office workers and young people alike for its reasonable prices. Known for its open-air street food stall atmosphere.

name: Gwangjang Market Park's Bindaetteok
description: A third-generation mung bean pancake stall inside Gwangjang Market. The signature bindaetteok, packed with mung beans and pork and pan-fried until crispy, is the star dish. Ranked among the market's top three must-try foods alongside mayak gimbap and yukhoe, it's a fixture on foreign food-tour itineraries.

name: Itaewon Dukkeobi-jip
description: A Korean restaurant that has held its ground in Itaewon for over 30 years. Doenjang-jjigae and cheonggukjang are the signature dishes, known for their deep, hearty flavor. With many foreign customers, an English menu is available, and prices are reasonable.

name: Jinjin Chinese Restaurant
description: A Michelin Guide-listed Chinese restaurant in Buam-dong, Jongno-gu. Famous for its modern take on jjajangmyeon and sweet and sour pork. Reservations are essential, and weekend slots are known to book out weeks in advance.

name: Onjium Food Space
description: Authentic royal-court-style Korean table d'hote served in a traditional hanok in Bukchon Hanok Village. The signature 12-dish table setting is made with seasonal ingredients, with traditional cooking methods behind every dish. Also runs Korean food culture experience programs for foreign visitors.

name: Downtowner Seongsu-dong Handmade Burgers
description: The Seongsu-dong burger joint that kickstarted Korea's handmade burger craze. The combination of a thick, flame-grilled patty and fresh vegetables is a hit, and the fries and milkshakes are popular too. You can watch the whole process from the open kitchen.
